world.title: SIGNIS: Rwanda Government Commends AMECEA’s Plenary as Catholic World Congress Opens in Kigali
world.description:
Sr. Jecinter Antoinette Okoth, FSSA
At the ongoing SIGNIS congress in Kigali, the Government of Rwanda has praised the recent plenary assembly of the Association of Member Episcopal Conferences in Eastern Africa (AMECEA), describing it as a timely call for the Church to walk alongside young people, pursue justice, and protect the environment.
The commendation came from Dr. Felicien Usengu Mucheza, Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Rwanda Governance Board, who delivered remarks on behalf of the Government of Rwanda at the opening of the first-ever Congress of the World Catholic Association for Communication (SIGNIS), held under the theme Digital Communication for Cultural Harmony and Environmental Well-being.
SIGNIS,  the World Catholic Association for Communication, is a non-governmental organization with over 100-member countries whose mission is to engage with media professionals and support Catholic Communicators to help transform cultures in the light of the Gospel by promoting human dignity, justice and reconciliation.
“This congress (SIGNIS) comes at a pivotal moment, closely following the recent plenary assembly of the Association of Member Episcopal Conferences in Eastern Africa where the bishops have made it clear that the Church must accompany young people, build bridges of justice and champion the care of our common home,” the Government representative said to nearly 300 participants from across the globe on Tuesday, August 4.
He emphasized that communicators are the bridge builders who “hold the megaphone that can translate pastoral priorities into messages that resonate across the globe.”
“I challenge you, over the coming days of dialogue and networking, to both reimagine the future of Catholic media,” he said.
Addressing the theme of the congress, the Deputy CEO also cautioned against the risks of an unregulated digital environment, and warned that algorithms designed to maximise engagement are fuelling division and misinformation. He called on communicators to champion transparency in Artificial Intelligence, resist data exploitation and ensure digital spaces remain safe and inclusive, while also urging the media to use film, radio, journalism and digital platforms to expose environmental injustice and amplify the voices of communities most affected by climate degradation.
He reaffirmed that the Rwanda Governance Board, which coordinates the work of non-governmental and faith-based organisations in the country, remains committed to partnering with such groups to advance good governance, ethical education, social transformation aligned with Vision 2050, and inclusive service delivery for vulnerable communities.
Dr. Mucheza further commended the Episcopal Conference of Rwanda and its partners for organising the Congress and formally declared the Congress, with participants from over 40 countries, officially opened in Rwanda’s capital Kigali.

science.title: High-accuracy structural modeling of antibody-antigen complexes
science.description: Accurate modeling of antibody-antigen complexes is crucial for advancing therapeutics and diagnostics, yet predicting their binding interface remains a formidable challenge. To address this, we introduce DeepAAAssembly, a protocol that enhances static predicted structural information by integrating dynamic interaction patterns to guide complex assembly. Our approach leverages predicted inter-chain residue distances to construct a flexibility-aware energy function, which drives a two-stage conformational sampling process for global exploration and local exploitation. On a benchmark set of 67 representative antibody-antigen complexes, by incorporating a built-in confidence selection mechanism, DeepAAAssembly outperforms AlphaFold3, not only consistently improving the quality of most targets, achieving an average DockQ score increase of 10.7%, but also reliably raising the accuracy of the most challenging cases from incorrect to acceptable levels. Furthermore, when applied to antibody-antigen targets in the CASP16 and CASP15 benchmark sets, the average DockQ score of DeepAAAssembly showed a 16.4% improvement compared to AlphaFold3. These results demonstrate that DeepAAAssembly effectively captures conserved interaction motifs and conformational flexibility, offering a robust framework for high-accuracy antibody-antigen modeling. DeepAAAssembly enhances antibody-antigen complex modeling by integrating deep learning-based distance prediction with a global exploration and local exploitation conformational sampling strategy.
